{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The question is about getting a first paying customer within 90 days. Idea B names a specific customer pair (a Wisconsin public adjuster and an affiliated roofing contractor) with a documented, narrow pain. Idea A has no identified buyer at all, so it would start from cold acquisition.",
    "B's price hypothesis rests on four directly comparable vendors with sourced pricing aimed at the same buyer: ClaimWizard at $99–$250/mo, Claim Titan from $82.50/mo, claimOS at $199/mo plus $99/user, and AdjustCRM at $65/user. That is direct evidence buyers in this niche already pay for this kind of software.",
    "A's core feature is offered free by Microsoft Quick Assist and JoinByKey. A's own Case against admits the value proposition has 'essentially zero price floor to beat.'",
    "A's realistic paying buyers, per its own brief, are support teams in healthcare, insurance and fintech. They likely require SOC 2, a HIPAA BAA and SSO before any deal, which threatens a 90-day first sale. B's compliance burden is real (Wisconsin's Insurance Data Security Law and breach-notice rules) but is mainly scoped as process and notice obligations, not a third-party certification gate.",
    "B's main weaknesses do not decide a first-customer bet. A tiny in-state market (188 licensed adjusters) and a crowded field limit scale, but not the first sale. A's weaknesses (free substitutes and an unproven payer segment) go straight at whether anyone pays at all."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence comes entirely from people helping elderly family members (an Apple Support Community thread and an r/it post about older parents). None of it comes from the support-team managers the brief names as the payer, so it does not show that the paying segment exists or would pay. In addition, the '41% faster resolution, 47% higher first-contact resolution' figures in A's Case for have no source and count as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's biggest advantage, the named customer, is undercut by B's own open question asking whether that commitment is real or informal; if it is informal, much of B's edge disappears. B also faces scope creep toward full claim-lifecycle features that incumbents already offer with AI extraction, and AdjustEdge's pricing could not be verified. Even so, A's free substitutes and its demand evidence from non-payers make it the weaker first bet."
}
